summary: Phantom generation observed live during the MPI-342 sweep: one requested Qwen Image Edit produced TWO jobs - qwenEdit_001 plus an unrequested appHeadSwap_002 (896x1152, 9s), toast '2 generations finished'. app.log has two 'Applied injector headSwap' lines 8.5 min apart (16:33:39Z deliberate, 16:42:12Z phantom), proving the second dispatch originated in the APP, not in a Pod queue replay. Root cause unknown - commandExecutor logs the injector but not the dispatch origin. Unknown whether it predates 0.28. Candidates (unconfirmed): stale app-op state after leaving the Head Swap workspace, a lane/queue leftover, or a reuse/CUE re-fire. First step: add dispatch-origin logging, then repro LOCALLY (free, and qwen-edit is installed locally).

Pod-side log captured before the Pod was deleted, and it sharpens the lead. The phantom job was a REAL tracked submission: it had its own prompt id (a1b6c045-cc4f-4b21-8bfc-cc155f4f2def) and the APP polled /wrapper/history for that id, so the app submitted it and followed it to completion - not a UI duplicate or a history-replay artifact. Crucially it ran 4 STEPS, the same as the deliberate appHeadSwap_001 which used the Hyper tier: the phantom carried the SAME parameters as the earlier job. That favours a REPLAY of the previous job (queue/lane leftover or reuse re-fire) over 'stale state built a new op', and is the strongest lead for the repro. Prompt executed in 8.52 seconds.

note: Root cause found by code read (no repro needed): MpiBaseApp binds Hotkeys generation.run at SETUP, but closing an app only HIDES its overlay - the shell destroys the instance only when a DIFFERENT app opens. So the closed Head Swap app kept a live Ctrl+Enter handler; the next Ctrl+Enter in the main workspace fired BOTH the PromptBox run and the stale app _run, enqueuing a second job from the still-persisted s_appInputs. Fixing by destroying the app instance on close.

FIXED. Root cause: MpiBaseApp binds the global generation.run hotkey at setup, but closing an app only HID the overlay - the shell destroyed the instance only when a DIFFERENT app opened. HotkeyManager fires ALL handlers bound to an id, so the next Ctrl+Enter ran the PromptBox run AND the closed app _run, re-submitting the persisted s_appInputs. Explains every observation (same params, real prompt id, injector logged 8.5 min later = the phantom dispatched when the 1m41s Qwen edit drained the single remote lane). Fix: the app emits close outward and the shell DESTROYS the instance on it (every open remounts fresh), killing all stale listeners. Proven live on the real Electron shell by tests/desktop/app-close-destroys-instance.spec.js - passes with the fix, FAILS (Expected 0, Received 1) with both source files stashed. Blast radius swept: all 30 Hotkeys.bind sites; MpiBaseApp was the only hidden-but-alive holder of a global hotkey. Not re-staged end-to-end (needs a Pod + Head Swap session) - the mechanism is proven in both directions instead. Detail in validation.md.
